data.title: Ecolab upgraded at Wells Fargo, touting CoolIT and Ovivo acquisitions
data.description:
Ecolab rose 1.8% in Friday's trading as Wells Fargo upgraded the water treatment and technology companies to Overweight from Equal Weight with a $380 price target, raised from $315, saying the CoolIT and Ovivo acquisitions shift the company to more attractive, high-growth end markets, while the Life Sciences business maintains its strength on easing capacity constraints.

CoolIT significantly expands Ecolab's Cooling-as-a-Service data center opportunity,positioning the company to benefit from both new data center builds and existing facility conversions to direct-to-chip cooling, which Wells Fargo's Jason Haas believes is less than 20% penetrated but rapidly growing as rack densities rise.

The analyst noted CoolIT more than doubled in growth between Q1 and Q3 2026, with continued upside as it leverages Ecolab's existing data center relationships and chemistry and service expertise to create a differentiated, end-to-end offering.

Meanwhile, Haas said Ovivo positions Ecolab to service the full fab lifecycle, extending its offering directly into ultra-pure water for chip production, setting up the company to benefit from both accelerating fab construction, with ~70 new fabs expected by 2030, and rising fab water-recycling needs, as semiconductor water demand is expected to grow more than 600% by 2050.

Haas said Ecolab's mission-critical services, long-standing customer relationships, and value-based pricing create a receptive customer base primarily focused on continuity of supply, adding that the company's FY 2022 energy surcharge remained in place for six quarters with relatively sticky volumes, while the Middle East conflict has represented a ~1% volume headwind.

data.title: Canada's Stelco to recall 175 laid-off workers, restart Hamilton plant finishing lines
data.description:
Canadian steelmaker Stelco said on Friday it will recall on December 1 all 175 workers who were temporarily laid off at its Hamilton, Ontario, plant and restart finishing operations after reaching deals with enough customers.

The country's steel industry, among the first and hardest hit by US President Donald Trump's import tariffs, has started to recover on the back of mining, energy and AI data center projects and government support, though the recovery has been uneven.

Here are more details:

  • CBC News reported in September that US-based steelmaker Cleveland-Cliffs would idle some production at its Hamilton, Ontario, plant and lay off hundreds of workers, blaming the damage done by US tariffs

  • Cleveland-Cliffs bought Stelco in 2024. The Canadian company makes flat-rolled steel, including coated, cold-rolled and hot-rolled products, as well as pig iron and metallurgical coke

  • Canada's response to Trump's tariffs has drawn global attention, with Prime Minister Mark Carney among the few leaders to hit back at Washington despite his country's heavy reliance on the US economy

  • Stelco said all affected employees will also be paid retroactively for the standard wages they missed during the temporary layoff

data.title: Uber Says Personal Data Was Exposed in Third-Party Data Breach — Update
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Uber Technologies is notifying users that their personal information was exposed in a breach involving one of the company's service providers.

The transportation company said an unauthorized third party had compromised a service provider's internal credentials and used them to access Uber's account, according to a notice on the California attorney general's website dated Tuesday.

"The notices to drivers are in relation to a security incident impacting one of our third-party vendors, Fireworks.ai, which had access to some Uber data," an Uber spokesperson said in a comment.

Uber immediately severed data connections with the service provider and launched an investigation after being notified about the breach Oct. 9.

Four days later, the investigation determined the unauthorized party had used the compromised credentials to access Uber data connected to the service provider.

Uber is providing affected individuals with access to credit monitoring and fraud assistance at no charge, according to the notice.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.

data.title: Meta Testing New Prediction-Market App With Employees — WSJ
data.description:
By Meghan Bobrowsky

Meta Platforms employees have begun testing a prediction-market app under development, according to people familiar with the matter, a step the company often takes ahead of a public release.

On the app, which is currently called Takes, employees can wager on the outcome of questions or events using "cred," short for credibility, the people said. Unlike other prediction markets operated by Kalshi and Polymarket, Meta's app doesn't allow users to wager real money.

If an employee's wager is correct, they win "cred" points and if they're wrong, they lose them, the people said. The app isn't available to the public and it is unclear when, if ever, it will be released. Meta declined to comment on the app.

The company regularly tests new apps, products and features among employees before releasing them to the public in a process referred to as "dogfooding." Not all of the products and apps make it out of the testing phase, and names and features can change ahead of release.

On Thursday, one of the questions on the Meta Takes app was whether former Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook is going to be the next CEO of Nvidia, the people said. At the time, the majority of the voters wagered that Cook would not.

Another question was about who would win the popular trivia show "Jeopardy" on Friday night, the people said.

The New York Times previously reported that Meta Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg had directed a team at the company to create a prediction-market app. At the time, over the summer, it was internally called Arena.

Zuckerberg hasn't publicly talked about the prediction-market app but said in an internal meeting with employees in the spring that he and product chief Chris Cox had been talking about building as many as 50 new apps, according to a recording reviewed by The Wall Street Journal.

Prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket have risen in popularity in recent years, particularly among Gen Z users, a cohort Meta is trying to keep engaged with its product offerings.

Kalshi and Polymarket are facing a number of lawsuits from U.S. states accusing them of operating illegal gambling platforms. The companies have maintained that they are federally regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

In response to lawsuits brought by the state of New York, a Kalshi spokeswoman called the legal action taken by New York Attorney General Letitia James "political theater" and Polymarket's legal chief said the company would "fight for our users."

Polymarket has a data partnership with Dow Jones, the publisher of the Journal.

Write to Meghan Bobrowsky at meghan.bobrowsky@wsj.com

data.title: Adani Green Energy rejects allegations on Tarali PSP project, calls cost revision claim "completely misleading"
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 13 -- Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) on Friday rejected allegations regarding the Tarali Pumped Storage Project (PSP), stating that claims that the company sought to revise project costs downwards to diminish statutory obligations are "completely misleading."

In a media statement, a spokesperson for AGEL clarified the company's position on the project cost mentioned in the online proposal on the forest/wildlife portal.

"The allegation that the company sought to revise project costs downwards to diminish statutory obligations is completely misleading. The online proposal in the forest / wildlife portal was solely for site investigation purposes, while the State Board for Wildlife (SBWL) considered total project costs of Rs 5675 crore," the spokesperson said.

The company explained that since site investigation costs are around 1 per cent of project costs, a clarification was provided that Rs 56.75 crore represented solely the site investigation and survey costs for the online proposal.

"Since site investigation costs are around 1% of project costs, therefore clarification of the project Rs 56.75 crore representing solely the site investigations and survey costs, for the online proposal was provided," the statement said.AGEL also dismissed the allegation that the downward revision was intended to lower conservation costs.

"Secondly, the allegation that downward revision was intended to lower conservation costs is false," the spokesperson said.On the project's location and environmental impact, the company stated that the Tarali PSP is situated entirely on private, non-forest land and is located 3.2 kms away from the Koyna Wildlife Sanctuary.

"The Tarali PSP is situated entirely on private, non-forest land and 3.2 kms away from the Koyna wildlife sanctuary. It is outside the notified buffer zone of Sahyadri Tiger reserve and in no way impacts or fringes upon the tiger corridor or any notified Eco-Sensitive zone (ESZ)," the statement said.

"The project does not cause diversion of any protected areas, any reserve forest or notified ESZ," the spokesperson added.

data.title: Nvidia Scandal is Poking Real Holes in the AI Trade. But That Doesn't Mean it's Over. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Alex Rosenberg

Investors can weather a sex scandal. They can handle the defenestration of America's central corporate leader. But suggest that corporate demand for chips isn't as robust as previously thought, and they've got a big problem.

As you certainly know by now, Jensen Huang has been forced to resign as CEO of Nvidia. Nvidia had been the world's most valuable company until the New York Times reported on Oct. 29 that Huang had been the target of a Chinese spy plot, but it has now lost a quarter of its value since then, adding to the losses it suffered earlier in October.

What we find notable is that the stock market, including AI-exposed stocks, actually held up pretty well as Nvidia cratered. In the first four days of the week, as Nvidia dropped 11%, the company's closed competitor, Advanced Micro Devices, rallied 30%, and Broadcom was up 24%. But on Friday, it was a different story: Nvidia fell 4%, AMD dropped 11%, and Broadcom was down 6%.

Perhaps investors are taking seriously the idea that chip demand isn't quite as torrid as we'd thought. On Thursday night, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had driven Nvidia to offer financing, in a rather willy-nilly manner, to companies that were committing to buying its chips. The story seemed to confirm the worst fears about the "circular financing" (i.e., I'll give you money so you can buy my products) that has undergirded the incredibly swift buildout of AI infrastructure. Meanwhile, Bloomberg reported that Nvidia chips were being smuggled into China with the help of the Chinese executive with whom Huang was having an affair — a violation of U.S. trade restrictions that would be baffling if demand for Nvidia chips had been as strong as we've been led to believe.

If investors are doubting the story about demand that Huang's been weaving, it calls into question whether the stock is really as reasonably valued as it looks. Worse, this may prove to be just one example of how aggressively companies have used circular financing to juice their earnings, which leads to broader questions. With the S&P 500's forward price-earnings ratio sitting at 18.4 times, it has been hard to make the case that stocks are in a bubble. But what if we are instead in an "earnings bubble," where unnaturally elevated chip prices and accounting gimmickry are producing a deceptive picture of the "E" in that P/E ratio? And what happens when investors lose faith in what executives are telling them?

"Nvidia was the linchpin for all this circular financing, and if Nvidia goes down, that means everything else goes down," says Noel Smith, co-CIO at Kai Asset Management.

On the other hand, Nomura chief investment strategist Andy Goldberg points out that these types of arrangements are common across a variety of industries. "I do think that circular financing is worth keeping an eye on, because dominoes can happen, but the thing to look for is slowing demand — and we haven't seen that yet."

Goldberg says that user demand for compute continues to surge, and he's confident that corporate capital expenditures will continue to build at least through next year, likening the spending to "a locomotive that's not going to slow down."

This would clearly be good news for chip makers, AI-related construction companies, and the rest of the AI infrastructure ecosystem. "I think ultimately you're going to see this episode as a buying opportunity," Goldberg says.

Certain AI-exposed areas of the market have sold off powerfully in the past few weeks, thanks not only to the Nvidia drama and to broader AI questions, but also to the strong anti-data-center flavor of the election results. But it is notable that the broad market is holding in pretty well. The Nasdaq, while 9% off its October peak, actually gained 1.9% this week as it recovered some of last week's losses. The Dow is up 1.8% on the week, and the S&P 500 is 2% higher. (In fact, the S&P is essentially flat since July 31.)

This resilience is leading Warren Pies of 3Fourteen Research to get bullish on stocks again. "The market's worst fears have materialized," he writes, pointing to Huang's exit, Democrats' wins, and hot inflation data that will likely lead to Fed rate hikes. "Yet, price action has been encouraging and sentiment has reset," he writes. "With the bad news out of the way, it's time to play for a year-end rally," Pies concludes.

It's a sound call.

When we encouraged investors to find ways to buy the dip last week, we pointed out that sentiment was not exuberant, and the economy remains strong. If anything, sentiment has gotten un-exuberant-er, and the hot inflation data suggests that the economy remains on firm — perhaps too firm — footing. We have plenty of key events ahead; investors are particularly focused on Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO next week, as well as December's Fed decision. Nonetheless, it's hard to imagine the rest of the year being as eventful as the last two weeks.

Perhaps that will allow investors to focus on what matters — a development that could redound to the benefit of the bulls.

Write to Alex Rosenberg at alex.rosenberg@barrons.com

data.title: Incoming House Speaker Jeffries heckled at Democratic conference
data.description:
By Tim Reid

Hakeem Jeffries, set to become US House Speaker when Democrats take control of Congress in January, was heckled by protesters on Friday who accused him of being too timid to address the high cost of living that fueled voter frustration in the midterm elections.

Jeffries was speaking at a gathering of Democrats in Denver to debate the future direction of the party after it routed President Donald Trump's Republicans in the November 3 elections. About 10 hecklers shouted at Jeffries, a moderate, demanding new, more progressive party leaders.

The interruption came as long-simmering splits inside the party between moderates and a restive progressive wing were being laid bare, with some speakers urging cooperation with Trump next year, and others calling for confrontation and accountability and a bold populist economic agenda.

Both factions of the party claimed vindication in the Democratic midterm sweep, each arguing that voters had endorsed their vision for the party's future.

That fight is expected to intensify when Democrats assume control of Congress in January as moderates press for a focus on affordability and governability while progressives push for a more expansive legislative agenda that includes action on healthcare, housing and corporate power.

The protesters demanded an end to Trump's war on Iran, government-funded health care for all, and an arms embargo on Israel.

"We need new leadership," one of them shouted. "I am scared for my future."

Jeffries ignored the hecklers, and the moderator commented how calm he remained, especially after one protester started swearing at him. "Remember, y'all, I grew up in Brooklyn," Jeffries replied.

Jeffries was followed on stage by Massachusetts Senator Chris Van Hollen, a progressive, who announced on Friday that he will challenge more centrist Senator Chuck Schumer of New York for the party's top leadership job in the Senate.

When he told the crowd in Denver he was challenging Schumer, he received a standing ovation. The event was being hosted by Majority Democrats, which advocates for younger leaders but also against left-wing policies.

Democrats are projected to hold at least 255 seats to ​Republicans' 169 in the House, with 12 contests still ​undecided. In the Senate, the breakdown will be ⁠at least 55-44, with Democrats possibly gaining one more seat in Alaska when vote-counting is completed.

data.title: US extends shipping law waiver 90 days, to allow freer movement of oil, commodities
data.description:
President Donald Trump extended for 90 days a waiver of a shipping law to allow foreign-flagged ships to transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday.

Reuters reported on Thursday that industry sources said the administration would extend the waiver on the more than 100-year-old Jones Act.

It has been the longest waiver in the history of the shipping law.

The administration issued a blanket waiver in March, a month after the US launched the war on Iran, in an effort to lower oil and fuel prices. In August, it extended the waiver but mandated that decisions would be made on a case-by-case basis, a stipulation continued through the latest waiver.

The ⁠Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies and crewed by American workers. Allowing the waiver aims to lower gas, diesel and fertilizer prices driven up by the war on Iran by increasing shipping flexibility and reducing transport bottlenecks.

Since the waiver was issued in March, an additional 90 million barrels of petroleum, mostly refined, have been shipped between US ports, the White House said. The total includes 27 million barrels of gasoline, 26 million barrels of crude oil, and 6 million barrels of renewable fuels.

The length of waivers has been limited in the past as the Jones Act is supported by the domestic shipbuilding business, a powerful lobby across the country.

data.description:
CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Athabasca Oil Corporation (“Athabasca” or the “Corporation”) is pleased to announce that independent proxy advisory firms, including Institutional Shareholder Services (“ISS”), have recommended shareholders vote “FOR” the proposed plan of arrangement (the “Arrangement” or the “Transaction”) with Cenovus Energy Inc. (“Cenovus”).

  • The Board of Directors of Athabasca (the “Athabasca Board”) unanimously recommends that shareholders vote FOR the Transaction.
  • Shareholders are reminded to vote and make their election choice well in advance of the November 25, 2026 proxy voting and election deadlines.
  • Questions or Require Voting Assistance? Contact Athabasca’s proxy solicitation agent, Laurel Hill Advisory Group, by telephone at 1‑877‑452‑7184 (toll-free in North America), 1-416-304-0211 (outside North America), by texting “INFO” to either number, or by email to assistance@laurelhill.com. Visit www.atha.com/2026-special-meeting for more information.

Independent Third-Party Proxy Advisory Recommendations

ISS is an independent proxy advisory firm whose clients include some of the world’s leading institutional investors, among others, who rely on its objective and impartial analysis to help inform their voting decisions.

ISS stated that “The transaction makes strategic sense due to the certainty of value and immediate liquidity provided by the premium cash consideration, while the CVE share consideration also provides an opportunity for additional upside through ownership in the combined company.”

Athabasca Board Recommendation

ISS' recommendation to vote "FOR" the Arrangement is consistent with the unanimous recommendation of the board of directors of Athabasca. The Athabasca Board unanimously recommends that Athabasca Shareholders vote FOR the Transaction Resolution.

Vote Your Shares and Make Your Election Choice Today - Voting is Easy

The proxy voting deadline for shareholders is Wednesday, November 25, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. (Calgary time). Shareholders are encouraged to vote well in advance of the proxy voting deadline to ensure their vote is submitted in a timely manner. Athabasca shareholders may vote online, by telephone or any other methods provided in the form of proxy or voting instruction form included as part of the mailing of the management information circular.

How to Make a Consideration Election

Athabasca Shareholders have the option to elect to receive either the Cash Consideration, the Share Consideration or a combination of both. The Election Deadline for Athabasca Shareholders to make the consideration election is on November 25, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. (Calgary Time). Shareholders who do not make an election will be deemed to have elected to receive the Cash Consideration for their Athabasca Shares, subject to rounding and proration as set out in the Plan of Arrangement.

  • For Beneficial Shareholders. If you hold common shares of Athabasca (“Athabasca Shares”) through a broker or other financial intermediary, contact your broker/intermediary to provide your election instructions. Your broker/intermediary may establish earlier deadlines for making elections. Beneficial Shareholders are encouraged to contact their intermediary/broker as soon as possible.
  • For Registered Shareholders. If you hold Athabasca Shares directly in your name and represented by a share certificate or a DRS Advice, please complete the Letter of Transmittal and Election Form and return it along with any certificate(s) representing the Athabasca Shares held to Computershare, Athabasca’s Depositary. If your Athabasca Shares are represented by a DRS Advice, there is no requirement to submit the DRS Advice and only the completed Letter of Transmittal and Election Form is required.

The special meeting of Athabasca shareholders will be held on November 27, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. (Calgary time) in a hybrid format, allowing shareholders to attend in person or participate virtually. Meeting participation details, the management information circular and related meeting materials are available at www.atha.com/2026-special-meeting. Shareholders requiring assistance may contact Laurel Hill using the information provided below.

Shareholder Questions and Voting Assistance

If you have questions, including the procedures for voting, please contact Athabasca’s proxy solicitation agent:

Laurel Hill Advisory Group

Toll-free calls in North America at 1-877-452-7184 (1-416-304-0211 outside North America)

Text message by texting "INFO" to 416-304-0211 or 1-877-452-7184

Email at assistance@laurelhill.com

About Athabasca Oil CorporationAthabasca Oil Corporation is a Canadian energy company with a focused strategy on the development of thermal and light oil assets. Situated in Alberta’s Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin, the Company has amassed a significant land base of extensive, high quality resources. Athabasca’s light oil assets are held in a private subsidiary (Duvernay Energy Corporation) in which Athabasca owns a 70% equity interest. Athabasca’s common shares trade on the TSX under the symbol “ATH”. For more information, visit www.atha.com.

data.title: National Economic Council Director Hassett to leave White House
data.description:
National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett is expected to depart his role at the White House in the coming weeks, according to three people familiar, said Semafor.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who could hold both jobs, and his counselor, David Zervos, are among those being eyed to replace Hassett, the news site said.

During his tenure, Hassett served as the face of economic policy, including the fallout from the Iran war, the president's campaign against former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, and an executive order expanding access to retirement plans.

Hassett's expected departure would be the latest in a series of staffing changes hitting the Trump administration in recent weeks. Hassett's deputy, Ryan Baasch, left the White House at the end of September, while Trump more recently replaced his chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller. Moreover, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is facing scrutiny over his handling of export controls on AI chips.
